title: Cognitive behavior therapy vs. control conditions, other psychotherapies, pharmacotherapies and combined treatment for depression: a comprehensive meta-analysis including 409 trials with 52,702 patients
authors: Cuijpers P, Miguel C, Harrer M, Plessen CY, Ciharova M, Ebert D, et al.
population: 409 randomised trials (518 comparisons) of cognitive behavioural therapy for depression
funder: not stated: the article text read in PubMed Central carries no funding statement; the acknowledgements refer only to supplementary information at osf.io.
result: CBT against care as usual or waitlist g=0.79 (95% CI 0.70 to 0.89). Against pharmacotherapies, no significant difference in the short term, and larger effects for CBT at 6 to 12 months (g=0.34, 0.09 to 0.58), from a small number of trials and not significant in all sensitivity analyses. Combined treatment exceeded pharmacotherapy alone in the short term (g=0.51) and long term (g=0.32) but not CBT alone.
